notes.subject: נחמתי
notes.rationale: נחם can mean 'repent/be sorry' (KJV) or 'be comforted' — context of shame favors 'repented', as in 'mi sori long ol samting mi bin wokim'.

notes.subject: ספקתי על ירך
notes.rationale: Striking the thigh = grief/self-reproach gesture; kept literal as 'paitim han long lek' since Tok Pisin readers see the action.

notes.subject: בשתי / נכלמתי
notes.rationale: Paired near-synonyms of shame intensified by וגם — 'ashamed, yes even confounded'; rendered as graded 'mi sem yet… mi sem nogut tru'.

notes.subject: long ol samting mi bin wokim
notes.rationale: Hebrew נחמתי is bare; Tok Pisin needs the object of sorrow made explicit.

translation: Tru, bihain long taim mi kamap bek, mi sori long ol samting mi bin wokim; na bihain long taim mi kisim save, mi paitim han long lek; mi sem yet, na mi sem nogut tru, bilong mi karim sem bilong taim yong bilong mi.
